source.value: Let $f(x)$ be a function with $f(-1)=-1, f'(-1)=3, f''(-1)=-6$ and $f'''(-1)=6.$ What is the third-degree Taylor polynomial for $f(x)$ about $x=-1?$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-7115

source.question: e-7115
source.value:
The third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(-1)+{f}^{′}(-1)(x+1)+\frac{{f}^{″}(-1)}{2!}(x+1)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(-1)}{3!}(x+1)^{3} \\  & =f(-1)+{f}^{′}(-1)(x+1)+\frac{{f}^{″}(-1)}{2}(x+1)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(-1)}{6}(x+1)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We have been given the following set of values: 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) & =-1 \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =3 \\ {f}^{″}(-1) & =-6 \\ {f}^{‴}(-1) & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given values into our Taylor polynomial, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =-1+3(x+1)+\frac{(-6)}{2}(x+1)^{2}+\frac{6}{6}(x+1)^{3} \\  & =-1+3(x+1)-3(x+1)^{2}+(x+1)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value: Find the third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x) = \ln(1+x)$ about $x=0.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-741

source.question: e-741
source.value:
To find the third-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=0,$ we plug $a=0$ into the general formula to give

$$
P_3(x) = f(0) + f'(0)(x-0) + \dfrac{1}{2!}f''(0)(x-0)^2 + \dfrac{1}{3!}f'''(0)(x-0)^3.
$$

We need to compute $f(0),$ $f'(0),$ $f''(0),$ and $f'''(0),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x) & ⟹ &  & f(0) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+0)=0 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =(1+x)^{-1} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(0) & =(1+0)^{-1}=1 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-(1+x)^{-2} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(0) & =-(1+0)^{-2}=-1 \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =2(1+x)^{-3} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(0) & =2(1+0)^{-3}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug the results for $f(0),$ $f'(0),$ $f''(0),$ and $f'''(0)$ into our third-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =0+(1)(x-0)+\frac{1}{2!}(-1)(x-0)^{2}+\frac{1}{3!}(2)(x-0)^{3} \\  & =x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value: What is the coefficient of $(x-1)^3$ in the third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x) = e^{-2x}?$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-742

source.question: e-742
source.value:
The coefficient of $(x-1)^3$ is $\dfrac{1}{3!}f^{(3)}(1).$ Let's compute the necessary derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{-2x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-2{e}^{-2x} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =4{e}^{-2x} \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =-8{e}^{-2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{1}{3!}f^{(3)}(1) =\dfrac{1}{6} \left( -8e^{-2} \right) = -\dfrac{4}{3e^2}.
$$

So the coefficient of $(x-1)^3$ is $-\dfrac{4}{3e^2}.$
